newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's 1995-96 coffee crop up 18 percent.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's 1995-96 coffee crop up 18 percent.

text.p: Venezuela's coffee crop rose 18 percent to 75.9 million kg, or approximately 1.265 million 60 kg bags, in the 1995-96 campaign ending September 30, the National Coffee Fund (Foncafe) said Thursday.
Foncafe director Ramon Hernandez told a news conference the figures resulted from better use of existing plantations and from a wide-ranging plan to revive the ailing industry.
He predicted the next campaign's crop would register "a 25 percent drop because of the extension of the rainy season". The country has been battered by unseasonal rains in the past weeks.
But Hernandez said Venezuela, which used to be among the world's top coffee exporting countries, hoped to reach "historic levels" in the 1997-98 campaign with output of up to 92 million kg.
He explained this objective could be reached thanks partly to the planting of 25,000 new hectares of coffee, a more than 10 percent increase on the current planted areas.
